title: fix(metadata-protocol): an orphan adoption hands each adopted object's registry owner and definition to the target package in the same request (#23646)
body:
Fixes #23646

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`reassignOrphanedMetadata` is the method `POST /api/v1/packages/:id/adopt-orphans` calls (ADR-0070 D5). It rebinds every package-less `sys_metadata` row to the target package Q. Its registry write-through followed view rows only. So an adopted object kept two things until a restart: the `sys_metadata` sentinel as its registry owner, and its pre-adoption definition. Meanwhile a save naming Q answered 200 and never went live.

Each adopted **active** object row now goes through two steps in the same request:

1. `releaseAdoptedObjectOwner` (a new private helper beside the method) removes the sentinel's registration. It calls the existing `SchemaRegistry.unregisterObject`, the verb the delete heal already uses to hand an object's name to a remaining row.
2. The row registers at its new binding through `applyRegistryWriteThrough`, the same write-through a save uses.

The registry holds one owner per object throughout (ADR-0029 D3). The adoption's request, its response and the set of rows it rebinds are unchanged.

- **Landing point:** `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, as the claim expected.
- **No registry verb was added** in `packages/objectql`. The hand-over is the existing `SchemaRegistry.unregisterObject` followed by the save's write-through. This PR builds no owner re-key primitive, so there is nothing new for another card to reuse. #23514 remains open.
- **The object SAVE door is untouched:** `saveMetaItem`, `classifyObjectContribution` and the D9.9 refusal do not move.

What the helper does depends on who owns the adopted name in the registry. Every row below is pinned:

| Registered owner of the adopted name | What the adoption does |
|:--|:--|
| the sentinel (the adopted row's own registration) | unregisters it, then registers the row under Q |
| none | registers the row under Q, as the next boot would |
| another package's row (legacy residue beside it) | rebinds the row in storage only; the registry keeps that owner, as before |
| the sentinel, but another package extends the object | `unregisterObject` refuses; the registry keeps the sentinel until the next restart; one `console.error` names the object, the consequence and the remedy |

A **draft** object row is rebound in storage only, because the boot registers active rows only (`loadMetaFromDb`).

## The card's first acceptance line: the HTTP route, walked on a full composition

The route was walked over HTTP before the fix and again after it. The composition was `pnpm dev:crm -- --fresh -p 38461`, the CRM example with the runtime's package service mounted, under the seeded admin's session.

**Before.** The code was `origin/main` `57994c311f`; branch head `e8a22df1b` added only the new test file and the changeset.

1. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget`, naming no package, answered `200`: "Saved object 'qa_probe_gadget' (env-wide, state=active)". Two `POST /api/v1/data/qa_probe_gadget` answered `201`, `201`.
2. `POST /api/v1/packages/com.qa.q/adopt-orphans` answered `200` with `reassignedCount: 1`. The server log has no registry line for it.
3. `PUT /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget?package=com.qa.q`, adding a field `serial`, answered `200`: "Saved object … package=com.qa.q". The server log then reads: `[Protocol] registerObject failed for qa_probe_gadget: Object "qa_probe_gadget" is already owned by package "sys_metadata". Package "com.qa.q" cannot claim ownership.`
4. The metadata read follows storage. `GET /api/v1/meta/object/qa_probe_gadget` serves label "Gadget Q", `_packageId` `com.qa.q` and the fields `name` and `serial`.
5. The data plane does not follow. `POST /api/v1/data/qa_probe_gadget` with `serial` answered `400 INVALID_FIELD` ("Unknown field 'serial'"), and so did `GET /api/v1/data/qa_probe_gadget?serial=S-3`.

**After.** The head was `535cd8562`, with `metadata-protocol` rebuilt.

- Steps 1–4 answer the same.
- At step 2 the server log now reads `Unregistered object: qa_probe_gadget (1 contribution(s), owner sys_metadata)` and then `Registered object: qa_probe_gadget (own, priority=100) from com.qa.q`.
- At step 3 it logs `… from com.qa.q`, with no refusal.
- At step 5 the `POST` with `serial` answered `201`, and `GET …?serial=S-3` answered `200` with `total: 1`.

A boot after that cannot be walked over HTTP, because `--fresh` storage is deleted on exit. The pins below hold the boot half at protocol level.

## Pins

The pins are in `packages/objectql/src/protocol-adopt-orphans-object-registry.test.ts`. They run on a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin` and a memory driver; another kernel booted over the same store is the reboot.

- Adopt, then read: owner Q, the data plane's definition stamped Q, one owner, and Q's package filter lists the object. This holds for an object saved in this process and for one hydrated at boot.
- A save naming Q after the adoption goes live: its new field is on the data plane at once, and a record using it inserts.
- A boot after that agrees.
- An adopted draft object row registers nothing.
- An object another package extends keeps its owner, said once at `error` naming the object and Q.
- CONTROL: an adoption of non-object items leaves the object registry untouched (no `registerObject` and no `unregisterObject` call), and the view follows as before.
- CONTROL: a package-less row of an object another package's row owns is rebound in storage, and the registry keeps that owner. Nothing of the residue is registered.

**Fixture triage.** One existing case in `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.object-registry-write-through-spelling.test.ts` pinned the defect: "an orphaned `objects` row not at all", with `registeredObjects` empty. It now pins the fold the new object limb applies: a row stored as `objects` registers under `object`, never under the plural. The `applyRegistryWriteThrough` call-site count stays 7, because the object limb rides the adoption's one existing call.

## Ablations (final code head `3061f6f3b`)

`objectql`'s tests import `metadata-protocol` through `dist/`. So each leg mutated the source through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor had to hit), rebuilt the package and proved the marker reached `dist/` with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`.

- **A — object limb removed.** The admission `type !== 'object'` was mutated, so objects skip again, as on `main`.
  - The tsup JS bundles built. Its DTS stage refused the mutant with TS2367: the narrowed `'view' | …` union makes `type === 'object'` unreachable, the mutant's own signature. The preflight read "marker present in 2 built files" (`index.js`, `index.cjs`).
  - Pin file: **3 failed | 3 passed.** The two adopt cases and the extender case went red. The draft case and both CONTROLs stayed green, by design.
  - Expected red, observed red.
- **B — active-row gate neutralised.** `row.state !== 'active'` was changed to a comparison that never holds.
  - Build exit 0; the preflight found the marker in 2 built files.
  - Pin file: **1 failed | 5 passed**, the draft case.
  - Expected red, observed red.
- **Restore.**
  - The blob `3a0c26243aa1` equals HEAD, and `git diff HEAD` on the path is empty.
  - The rebuild exited 0, and both markers are absent from all 24 built files.
  - The working tree is clean, and the pin file reads **6 passed**.

## Tests (local)

These ran at `7d0b4d97d`, the branch merged with `origin/main` `547702080`, which includes #23659's delete heal:

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol typecheck`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test`: 236 files passed and 3 skipped; 20563 tests passed and 19 skipped.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` reports OK; the new file adds no debt.
- `objectql` protocol suites, 8 files, 74 passed: the new pin file, `protocol-package-lifecycle`, `protocol-writepath-object-ownership`, `protocol-runtime-owner-overlay-refusal`, `protocol-boot-object-package-binding`, `protocol-object-overlay-layer`, `protocol-boot-hydration-scoped` and `protocol-delete-boot-hydrated-object-heal`.
- `runtime` `package-duplicate-adopt-org-scope.integration.test.ts`: 4 passed.

These ran at `3061f6f3b`: the pin file, 6 passed, and the `objectql` typecheck, exit 0. The last commit `9e2c7a578` only types the pin file's data-plane read options (`EngineReadOptions` in place of an `as any`). After it, `check:query-options-erasure` holds at 236 test sites, the ceiling.

## Gates (local)

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `9e2c7a578` derived 67 commands.
- All 67 ran on that head. Each exit code was captured before any pipe: **67 × exit 0**.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "67 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- `check:type-check-debt` ran inside one verify-lock hold, because its closure build needs the lock.
- The first union, at `3061f6f3b`, had two non-zero results, both superseded by the `9e2c7a578` run:
  - `check:query-options-erasure` was red: the test surface grew 236 → 237 through the pin file's `as any` on a read's options. `9e2c7a578` fixed it.
  - `check:type-check-debt` answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` because it got no turn on the lock.
- CI runs its full battery on this PR.

## Acceptance notes

- **Finding, handed to the seat to file.** The adoption's existing view limb registers a **draft** package-less view row as live. This was measured on a real `ObjectKernel` with `ObjectQLPlugin`; the view limb is byte-identical to `main`.
  - Before the adoption, `registry.getItem('view', NAME)` answered nothing.
  - After it, the registry serves the draft body, bound to Q, while the stored row is still `state: draft`.
  - The boot registers active rows only.
  - This PR does not touch the view limb; the CONTROL above pins it as unchanged.
- **Legacy residue.** Suppose a package-less row sits beside another package R's row of the same object. The adoption rebinds the package-less row into Q in storage, so two rows of one object are bound to two packages, a shape the registry cannot hold (D9.9). The registry keeps R, as before. The next boot judges both rows (not measured here). This behaviour predates this PR.
- **The extender refusal is logged at `error`, not `warn`.** By AGENTS.md's degradation question, storage and the runtime disagree while the adoption answers success. The remedy the line names is a restart.
